newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney says 1997 looks challenging.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney says 1997 looks challenging.

text.p: Euro Disney chairman Philippe Bourguignon said a weak spending climate, coupled with the Disneyland Paris theme park operator's rising financial charges, posed a challenge for 1997.

"Persistent weakness in the economy, constant pressure on our prices, and the strong increase in financial charges constitute several real challenges for the future, particularly in 1997," he said in the company's full-year earnings statement.
"One thing is certain: our public endorsement is definitely demonstrated," he said. Euro Disney reported a 77 percent jump in 1995-96 profit and record attendance of 11.7 million people.
Lease and financial charges for the year to September 30, 1996, rose by 103 million francs to 568 million as the costs of a 1994 six billion franc financial restructuring were gradually phased in.
The company previously estimated the rise in financial charges at 100 million francs for 1995/96, 200 million for 1996/97, and another 100 million for 1997/98.
From 1998/99, royalties and management fees to 39 percent owner The Walt Disney Co will also be reinstated.

Euro Disney said a strong operating performance in the year just ended more than offset the rise in financial charges. This resulted in a surge in 1995-96 income before exceptional items to 156 million francs from two million the previous year.
Net income rose to 202 million francs from 114 million in 1994-95, when the company first emerged from the red after losing more than seven billion francs in its first two years.
